title: Design System: symcc board in Cursor

coral-wash.canonical: color-mix(in srgb, var(--coral) 8%, var(--bg)); 9% in light themes

coral-edge.canonical: color-mix(in srgb, var(--coral) 45%, var(--line)); high contrast: var(--vscode-contrastActiveBorder)

raised.canonical: color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 4%, var(--bg)); 3% in light themes

raised-2.canonical: color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 7%, var(--bg)); 6% in light themes

headline.purpose: Empty and setup screen headings only.

title.purpose: Project name in the header; Board and Scouts page headings.

card-title.purpose: Decision card and scout headings, clamped to three lines.

body.purpose: Stream text and the default for everything; messages to 72ch.

body-small.purpose: Card text, buttons, header counts, news rows, side lists.

label.purpose: Section headings: Needs you, Running, Up next, Board groups. Sentence case.

caption.purpose: Timestamps, day dividers, composer hint, tags.

micro.purpose: Rail labels and staff station words.

mono.purpose: Task ids, file paths, inline and fenced code; 11.5px in file lists.

shadows.name: notice-float
shadows.purpose: The transient notice under the header. The only shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for the staff slide and the notice rise.

motion.name: staff-slide
motion.purpose: The current note and the passed segment move to the next station.

motion.name: breathe
motion.value: 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; opacity 0.15 to 0.7, scale 0.85 to 1.1
motion.purpose: The ring around the current note while an agent works.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No slide, no breathing (ring held at 45%), no notice rise.

breakpoints.name: fold-side
breakpoints.purpose: Side column becomes a Running strip above the stream; Now scrolls as one column; composer sticky.

breakpoints.name: rail-top
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes a 44px top bar; cards one column; 14px gutters.

narrative.overview:
The panel is a lead sheet pinned beside the editor: the melody (what needs the owner) is written large and in coral at the top, the accompaniment (the lead's conversation and the board's news) runs underneath as one quiet timeline, and each running task is read like a bar of music on a single staff line. Everything that is not the melody belongs to the host editor. Ground, text, borders, inputs, focus rings, links, scrollbars and selection are the editor theme's own `--vscode-*` values, so the panel looks native in dark, light and high-contrast themes and only the symcc layer is fixed.

That layer is small and deliberate: a deep navy-to-plum rail carrying the treble-clef mark on its coral tile, coral reserved for what needs the owner and the one primary action on each card, and a green / amber / red / blue state vocabulary borrowed from the host's chart colors. Density is editor density (13px body, 28px controls, 8 to 20px gaps), calm and scannable rather than spacious. Depth is tonal, built by mixing a few percent of the foreground into the ground.
keyCharacteristics: Host-themed ground and controls; symcc owns only the rail, the mark, coral and the staff.
Coral is scarce: decisions waiting, the primary action per card, the current note, the rail count.
One timeline: messages and board news share a single stream, newest at the bottom, composer pinned below.
The staff line is the signature: stations as notes, passed notes green, the current note coral and breathing.
Codicons for every icon, in the host's icon font.

rules.name: The Coral Means You Rule
rules.body: Coral marks only what needs the owner and the single primary action on a card. Running work, progress and success are never coral.

rules.name: The Borrowed Ground Rule
rules.body: Ground, text, borders, inputs, focus, links, selection and scrollbars come from `--vscode-*` variables with a fallback. symcc hard-codes only coral, the rail and the mark.

rules.name: The Two Corals Rule
rules.body: Coral as a fill uses `coral`; coral as text uses the theme-switched coral text value. Never set text in the fill coral.

rules.name: The Host Voice Rule
rules.body: Use the editor's UI font for all prose and controls and the editor's code font for ids, paths and code. Do not load a web font.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates or lines up (counts, times, line deltas, lane meta) is set with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Tonal Step Rule
rules.body: To raise a surface, mix more foreground into the ground (`raised`, then `raised-2`) and give it the host line; do not add a shadow.

dos: Do take every neutral from a `--vscode-*` variable with a fallback, so dark, light and high-contrast themes all hold.
Do keep coral to what needs the owner: the Needs you heading and cards, one primary button per card, the rail count and the current note.
Do switch coral text between #f2a58a on dark and #a8482a on light; lay text on coral fills in clef ink (#1b1f2a).
Do draw every icon with a codicon (`git-branch`, `pass`, `loading`, `send`, `warning`); a busy control swaps its icon for `loading`.
Do raise surfaces tonally (4% then 7% foreground into the ground) with a 1px host line.
Do show task progress as notes on the staff, green for passed and coral for the current station, with motion turned off under reduced motion.
Do set counts, times and line deltas in tabular numerals, and ids, paths and code in the editor's code font.
donts: Don't color running work, progress or success coral; those are blue and green.
Don't hard-code a ground, text, border or focus color outside the rail and the mark.
Don't load a web font or set prose in the code font.
Don't add shadows to cards, lanes or buttons; the notice float is the only shadow.
Don't put a bar down one side of a card or row to mark state; use the wash, the full border or the state word.
Don't place a label above a heading; headings such as "Needs you" and "Running" stand alone.
